concepts.title: Powers with Negative Exponents
concepts.definition: A negative exponent means reciprocal: 10 to the minus 2 equals 1 over 100, and a to the minus m equals 1 over a to the m for any nonzero base, extending powers naturally below one.
concepts.key_idea: Negative power, positive sense: flip the base into the denominator.
question_patterns: find the value of 2 to the power minus 4
write 10 to the minus 3 as a fraction
evaluate the given negative power
what is the reciprocal of 5 to the power 3 as a power
express 1/64 as a power of 2 with a negative exponent
find the multiplicative inverse of 7 to the minus 2

solution_steps.explain: Compute the base raised to the exponent size.
The negative exponent is 1 over that power.

concepts.title: Laws of Exponents
concepts.definition: Powers obey compact laws for any nonzero base: multiplying powers adds exponents, dividing subtracts them, a power of a power multiplies exponents, and equal exponents multiply or divide the bases - rules that hold for negative exponents too.
concepts.key_idea: Same base adds exponents; same exponent operates on the bases.
question_patterns: simplify 2 to the 3rd times 2 to the 4th
simplify and write in exponential form the given product
evaluate (3 to the 2nd) to the 3rd using laws of exponents
simplify the quotient of the two powers
use the laws of exponents to simplify the given expression
state the laws governing powers with the same base

solution_steps.explain: The product is the base to the summed exponent.

concepts.title: Standard Form for Very Large and Small Numbers
concepts.definition: Very large and very small numbers read best in standard form: a coefficient from 1 up to 10 times a power of 10, so the earth's mass of 5,976,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 kg becomes 5.976 times 10 to the 24 kg, and tiny sizes use negative powers.
concepts.key_idea: Count the decimal shifts: the exponent of ten records them exactly.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh110.txt section 10.4 (use of exponents to express small numbers in standard form)
question_patterns: express the mass of the earth in standard form
write the given large number in standard form
express 0.000007 in standard form
write the thickness of the given object in standard form
convert 5.976 times 10 to the 24 into an ordinary number
which is larger: the two given numbers in standard form

solution_steps.explain: 10 to the exponent gives the scale.
Coefficient times scale rebuilds the number.

concepts.title: Comparing Very Large and Very Small Numbers
concepts.definition: Standard form makes comparison easy: numbers with bigger exponents of ten are bigger regardless of the coefficient, and equal exponents are compared by their coefficients - which is why the exponent matters more than the digits.
concepts.key_idea: Compare exponents of ten first; only a tie sends you to the coefficients.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh110.txt section 10.4.1 (comparing very large and very small numbers)
question_patterns: compare the two given numbers written in standard form
which is greater: the given pair of very large numbers
arrange the given standard form numbers in increasing order
how many times bigger is the first number than the second
why does the exponent decide the size of a standard form number
compare the size of a cell with the given dimensions in standard form

solution_steps.explain: The larger power of ten wins outright.
Equal exponents fall to comparing coefficients.
Dividing the values shows how many times one exceeds the other.
